relations.myth: Ordering the cosmos after the eternal model
relations.note: The craftsman imitates the eternal model when forming the visible cosmos.

relations.myth: Intellect persuades Necessity during cosmic formation
relations.note: The craftsman’s intellect persuades Necessity to cooperate in forming the best possible cosmos.

relations.myth: Manufacture of the world-soul
relations.note: The craftsman mixes, divides, and places the world-soul before and within the cosmic body.

relations.myth: Generation of the celestial gods
relations.note: The craftsman constructs the celestial gods as components of the ordered living cosmos.

relations.myth: Delegation of mortal creation
relations.note: The craftsman instructs the younger gods to make mortal creatures while he supplies immortal soul.
Numenius’s second, demiurgic God derives from or depends upon the first God.

relations.myth: The second God imitates the first
relations.note: The demiurgic intellect participates in and imitates the first Good.

relations.myth: Marcion’s two gods
relations.note: Marcion’s creator governs this world but stands opposed and inferior to the good God.

relations.myth: Christ invades the creator’s domain
relations.note: Christ enters the creator’s jurisdiction from the good God and liberates those subject to it.
Sophia produces Yaldabaoth without her consort and hides her malformed offspring.

relations.myth: Yaldabaoth takes Sophia’s luminous power
relations.note: Yaldabaoth receives or seizes luminous power from Sophia, which later passes into Adam.

relations.myth: Higher fullness defeats Yaldabaoth’s exclusive claim
relations.note: Barbelo belongs to the divine fullness beyond Yaldabaoth’s knowledge that overturns his claim of sole divinity.

relations.myth: Higher fullness defeats Yaldabaoth’s exclusive claim
relations.note: The Invisible Spirit transcends Yaldabaoth and authorizes the higher order that exposes his ignorance.

relations.myth: The arrogant ruler’s boast is rebuked
relations.note: A divine voice refutes the ruler’s boast and announces an immortal human above him.
relations.source: Apocryphon of John; Hypostasis of the Archons

relations.note: Yaldabaoth generates subordinate authorities to govern the heavens and help form Adam.

relations.myth: The archons govern and form Adam
relations.note: The subordinate authorities obey Yaldabaoth, rule lower heavens, and assist his formation of humanity.

relations.myth: Providence descends into the ruler’s darkness
relations.note: Pronoia repeatedly enters the ruler’s darkness to awaken and save the imprisoned divine seed.

relations.myth: Epinoia aids Adam against the rulers
relations.note: Hidden within Adam, Epinoia corrects the archons’ deficiency and helps humanity attain knowledge.

relations.myth: Formation and animation of Adam
relations.note: Yaldabaoth and his rulers form Adam’s body, and Yaldabaoth’s breath inadvertently transfers divine power.

relations.myth: Adam is confined in paradise
relations.note: The ruler confines Adam in paradise and imposes prohibition and forgetfulness to maintain ignorance.

relations.myth: The rulers pursue Eve’s likeness
relations.note: The rulers attempt to assault Eve’s likeness, but the true spiritual Eve escapes their domination.
relations.source: Apocryphon of John; Hypostasis of the Archons

relations.myth: The instructor aids knowledge against the ruler
relations.note: In some Gnostic rereadings, the serpent promotes knowledge against the ruler, though its identity and evaluation vary.
relations.source: Hypostasis; Origin of the World; Ophite reports

relations.note: Sabaoth is Yaldabaoth’s son in On the Origin of the World.
relations.source: On the Origin of the World

relations.myth: Sabaoth’s revolt
relations.note: Sabaoth condemns and rejects his father Yaldabaoth, repents, and joins the superior powers.
relations.source: On the Origin of the World

relations.myth: Yaldabaoth envies Sabaoth’s promotion
relations.note: Yaldabaoth envies Sabaoth after Sophia and Zoe enthrone him above the lower powers.
relations.source: On the Origin of the World

relations.myth: Condemnation of the arrogant ruler
relations.note: Pistis Sophia rebukes and judges the arrogant ruler while establishing powers superior to him.
relations.source: On the Origin of the World

relations.myth: Nebro and Saklas generate subordinate angels
relations.note: Nebro/Yaldabaoth and Saklas emerge separately and cooperate in producing subordinate rulers.
The Valentinian Demiurge arises from psychic substance produced by Sophia or Achamoth.

relations.myth: Achamoth secretly guides cosmic formation
relations.note: The Demiurge unknowingly serves Achamoth’s hidden governance while fashioning the lower cosmos.

relations.myth: The Savior reveals the higher Pleroma
relations.note: The Savior brings higher knowledge, and the Demiurge eventually learns that powers exist above him.

relations.myth: Powers of the right oppose the Devil
relations.note: The just Valentinian Demiurge and powers of the right oppose the Devil and powers of the left.
relations.source: Letter to Flora; Excerpts from Theodotus

relations.note: Plotinus locates demiurgic formation in the eternal productive activity of Intellect rather than an ignorant craftsman.
Plotinus treats Soul as an eternal productive and ordering agency within the demiurgic hierarchy.
Sethian and related traditions identify Yaldabaoth as a hostile or arrogant demiurgic chief ruler.
relations.source: Apocryphon of John; Gospel of Judas

relations.note: The Apocryphon names Sakla as Yaldabaoth, although the Gospel of Judas treats Saklas separately.
Several Coptic texts identify the demiurgic ruler with Samael, reusing a Jewish angelological name.
relations.source: Apocryphon of John; Hypostasis of the Archons

relations.note: The Gospel of Judas identifies Nebro with Yaldabaoth while distinguishing him from Saklas.
Modern interpretation compares Blake’s oppressive world-forming lawgiver with the Demiurge without claiming historical identity.
relations.source: Blake, The First Book of Urizen
